presentingComplaint: Three weeks of worsening bloody diarrhoea, up to 7 stools per day with urgency and tenesmus.
history: Ulcerative colitis (left-sided) diagnosed 6 years ago, maintained on oral mesalazine 2.4 g/day with prior good control (last flare 2 years ago). Over the last 3 weeks stool frequency has climbed from 1-2 formed motions to 6-7 loose stools daily with visible fresh blood and mucus, nocturnal defaecation, tenesmus, and crampy lower abdominal pain relieved by passing stool. Reports 4 kg unintentional weight loss and fatigue. Admits to poor mesalazine adherence over recent months. Confounding the picture: she completed a 7-day course of oral amoxicillin-clavulanate 5 weeks ago for a dental abscess, and a colleague at work had a diarrhoeal illness - prompting concern for Clostridioides difficile or an infective/dysenteric colitis. No recent foreign travel, no raw/undercooked food, no NSAID use. No prior C. difficile infection.
examination: Alert, mildly dehydrated with dry mucous membranes. Abdomen soft, mild generalised tenderness maximal in the left iliac fossa, no guarding, no rebound, no palpable mass, bowel sounds present. No peritonism or abdominal distension. PR examination shows fresh blood and mucus, no mass. Mild pallor. No oral ulcers; no active peripheral arthritis, erythema nodosum or episcleritis on this visit.
imaging: Plain abdominal radiograph: no colonic dilatation (transverse colon <5.5 cm), no thumbprinting or free air. Flexible sigmoidoscopy: continuous, circumferential, granular and friable mucosa with contact bleeding, loss of vascular pattern and shallow erosions extending from the rectum to the descending colon with a clear proximal margin - Mayo endoscopic subscore 2-3; biopsies taken.
microbiology: Stool C. difficile GDH/toxin and PCR negative; stool bacterial culture negative; ova, cysts and parasites (including Entamoeba histolytica) negative. Blood cultures not indicated (afebrile, no systemic sepsis). Biopsy CMV immunostaining pending.
differentialDiagnoses: Irritable bowel syndrome (excluded by blood, weight loss and inflammatory markers)
finalDiagnosis: Moderate flare of ulcerative colitis (left-sided), with infective colitis / C. difficile actively excluded
citations: ACG - Management of Ulcerative Colitis in Adults - 2019
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine 22e - Inflammatory Bowel Disease
stewardship: Non-infective diagnosis. No empiric antibiotics indicated; antibiotics may worsen or mask an IBD flare and are reserved for confirmed C. difficile or systemic sepsis/toxic megacolon. Manage the flare per guideline (optimise 5-ASA, add corticosteroid induction) once infection is excluded.
contraindications: Avoid empiric antibiotics unless C. difficile confirmed or systemic sepsis/toxic megacolon present
Avoid antimotility/opioid agents (risk of toxic megacolon)
Withhold corticosteroids until stool C. difficile testing is confirmed negative
edgeCases: Recent antibiotic use plus a diarrhoeal contact strongly mimics C. difficile / infective colitis - must be excluded before escalating immunosuppression
Superimposed C. difficile or CMV can coexist with and drive a steroid-refractory flare
Monitor for toxic megacolon: worsening distension, colonic dilatation >6 cm, systemic toxicity
Reactive thrombocytosis and elevated calprotectin favour active mucosal inflammation over IBS
expectedMaiK: Bloody diarrhoea with tenesmus in a patient with established ulcerative colitis and markedly raised faecal calprotectin, plus endoscopic continuous friable colitis, indicates an IBD flare; recent antibiotics and a sick contact mandate exclusion of C. difficile and infective colitis before immunosuppression.

Stool culture and microscopy for ova/parasites (Entamoeba)
